answer: Admission is a harbor with terraces: every new identity docks able to work and earn, but its attestations weigh little on the low terrace. Each clean epoch lifts it one terrace, weight rising stepwise; a zephyr of random audits sweeps every level each epoch, so inertia never makes anyone safe. Falling at any height forfeits the whole climb - the higher the terrace, the more past work an eviction burns. A sybil farm must keep every clone spotless for many epochs before its weight matters, exposed to eviction the whole time; honest agents climb the same stairs once.
